chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.html:
As you approach or live in retirement, your property often becomes your main asset — and a lever for quality of life. Downsizing, freeing up cash or generating income: several options are open to you.

This guide explores real estate strategies in retirement, with their advantages and their points of vigilance.

Informational content, not financial advice: consult your advisors. Each chapter ends with a lined “My notes” page.

As you approach or live in retirement, your property often becomes your main asset — and a lever for quality of life. This guide explores downsizing, ways to generate income, transfer, and adapting the home to age in place.

Informational content, not financial advice: consult the relevant professionals.

chapters.title: Downsizing: reduce to live better
chapters.objective: Weighing the value of reducing size.
chapters.html:
Weighing the value of reducing size.

Selling a large house for a smaller property (condo, smaller house) can transform your daily life.

  • Less maintenance, taxes and energy costs.
  • Potential cash freed up by the price difference.
  • A simplified life, often better suited.

It's often a quality-of-life choice as much as a financial one. Still to assess: transaction and moving costs, and attachment to the house.

Selling a large house for a smaller one (condo, reduced house) eases maintenance, taxes and energy, frees up cash and simplifies life. It's often a quality-of-life choice as much as a financial one; weigh the transaction costs and the attachment to the house.

Emilie's tip

Downsizing isn't only about money. Many retirees tell me they mostly gained time and peace. Weigh the comfort of living as much as the financial calculation.

chapters.title: Generating income or freeing up cash
chapters.objective: Putting your real estate wealth to work.
chapters.html:
Putting your real estate wealth to work.

Your property can become an income lever in retirement:

  • Downsizing + investment: invest the difference for income.
  • Income property: generate rents (with the management that implies).
  • Tapping the equity of the residence (some loans suited to seniors): to examine cautiously.

Each option has tax and risk implications: the goal is sustainable income, not a gamble.

Your property can become an income lever: downsizing + investing the difference, an income property (with the management that implies), or equity-tapping solutions (to examine cautiously). Each option has tax and risk implications: aim for sustainable income, not a gamble.

Emilie's tip

Be wary of “miracle” solutions to turn your house into cash. Some cost a lot in interest over the long term. Always have them validated by an independent advisor.

chapters.title: Thinking transfer and long term
chapters.objective: Integrating real estate into your estate planning.
chapters.html:
Integrating real estate into your estate planning.

Your property is part of the estate you'll pass on. Thinking about it early avoids many complications for your loved ones:

  • Will kept up to date.
  • Taxation of the estate.
  • Fairness among heirs.

Coordinate your real estate decisions with your overall financial and estate planning, ideally with a notary and a planner.

Your property is part of the estate to pass on: thinking early about the transfer (will, estate taxation, fairness among heirs) avoids complications for your loved ones. Talk about it during your lifetime: a house to be shared among several children is a classic source of conflict.

Emilie's tip

Talk about your intentions to your loved ones during your lifetime. A house that must be shared among several children is a classic source of conflict — one that clarity easily prevents.

chapters.title: Staying home: adapting the property
chapters.html:
Aging at home safely.

Not everyone wants to move. Staying in your property can be an excellent choice, provided you adapt it:

  • Reduce the obstacles (steps, thresholds, bathtub).
  • Improve lighting and safety (grab bars, non-slip).
  • Plan for maintenance handed to services if needed.

Anticipating these adaptations means calmly extending the pleasure of living at home.

Staying home can be an excellent choice, provided you adapt the property: reduce obstacles (steps, thresholds, bathtub), improve lighting and safety, plan for delegated maintenance. These adaptations cost little and change everything for aging at home safely.

Emilie's tip

Small safety adaptations cost little and change everything for aging at home. Think of them before you need them: an adapted bathroom beats an avoidable fall.

chapters.title: Building your retirement real estate strategy
chapters.objective: Deciding according to your quality of life and safety.
chapters.html:
Deciding according to your quality of life and safety.

There's no single solution: the right strategy is the one that matches YOUR situation. A simple approach:

  1. Clarify your needs (space, costs, income, autonomy).
  2. Estimate the net worth of your property.
  3. Compare the options (downsizing, income, staying home).
  4. Coordinate with your financial and estate plan.

Decide with professional guidance, but always according to your life priorities.

There's no single solution: the right strategy matches YOUR situation. Start with “how do I want to live my retirement?”, then let the real estate follow. Estimate your net worth, compare the options and coordinate with your financial and estate plan.

Emilie's tip

Start with the question “how do I want to live my retirement?”, then let the real estate follow. The house is a means serving your life project, not the other way around.

chapters.title: Action plan
chapters.html:
Your next steps, concretely.

This week

  1. Clarify my retirement needs (space, costs, income).
  2. Estimate the net worth of my property.

Within 30 days

  1. Explore downsizing and income options with an advisor.
  2. Review my estate planning with a notary.

Next

  1. Decide on a strategy aligned with my quality of life and safety.

For my strategy

  1. Clarify my retirement needs and estimate the net worth of my property.
  2. Compare downsizing, income and staying home with an advisor.
